passages.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, and Timothy our brother, To the church of God in Corinth, together with all the saints throughout Achaia: Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Christ Jesus.
God chose Paul to be an apostle.
Timothy is our brother.
Paul and Timothy write this letter.
They write to the church of God in Corinth.
They also write to all the saints in all Achaia.
Paul and Timothy greet the church and the saints.
They say, “Grace to you.”
They say, “Peace to you.”
Grace and peace come from God our Father.
Grace and peace come from the Lord Jesus Christ.
passages.original: Παῦλος ἀπόστολος Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ διὰ θελήματος Θεοῦ καὶ Τιμόθεος ὁ ἀδελφὸς Τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ τοῦ Θεοῦ τῇ οὔσῃ ἐν Κορίνθῳ σὺν τοῖς ἁγίοις πᾶσιν τοῖς οὖσιν ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ Ἀχαΐᾳ Χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη ἀπὸ Θεοῦ Πατρὸς ἡμῶν καὶ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ

passages.text: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of compassion and the God of all comfort, who comforts us in all our troubles, so that we can comfort those in any trouble with the comfort we ourselves have received from God.
passages.sermon:
God is the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.
God is our Father.
God is full of compassion.
God gives all comfort.
God comforts us when we have troubles.
God does this so we can comfort others who have troubles.
We use the same comfort that God gave us to comfort them.
passages.original: Εὐλογητὸς ὁ Θεὸς καὶ Πατὴρ τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ὁ Πατὴρ τῶν οἰκτιρμῶν καὶ Θεὸς πάσης παρακλήσεως ὁ παρακαλῶν ἡμᾶς ἐπὶ πάσῃ τῇ θλίψει ἡμῶν εἰς τὸ δύνασθαι ἡμᾶς παρακαλεῖν τοὺς ἐν πάσῃ θλίψει διὰ τῆς παρακλήσεως ἧς παρακαλούμεθα αὐτοὶ ὑπὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: For just as the sufferings of Christ overflow to us, so also through Christ our comfort overflows.
passages.sermon:
The sufferings of Christ come to us in great measure.
We receive many sufferings because we follow Christ.
Through Christ, we also receive much comfort.
Our comfort overflows because of Christ.
Christ brings both suffering and comfort to us.
passages.original: ὅτι καθὼς περισσεύει τὰ παθήματα τοῦ Χριστοῦ εἰς ἡμᾶς οὕτως διὰ τοῦ Χριστοῦ περισσεύει καὶ ἡ παράκλησις ἡμῶν

passages.text: If we are afflicted, it is for your comfort and salvation; if we are comforted, it is for your comfort, which accomplishes in you patient endurance of the same sufferings we experience.
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul and his companions suffer for the sake of the believers.
If we suffer, it is for your comfort.
If we suffer, it is for your salvation.
If we receive comfort, it is for your comfort.
This comfort helps you endure suffering with patience.
You experience the same sufferings that we experience.
passages.original: Εἴτε δὲ θλιβόμεθα ὑπὲρ τῆς ὑμῶν παρακλήσεως καὶ σωτηρίας εἴτε παρακαλούμεθα ὑπὲρ τῆς ὑμῶν παρακλήσεως τῆς ἐνεργουμένης ἐν ὑπομονῇ τῶν αὐτῶν παθημάτων ὧν καὶ ἡμεῖς πάσχομεν

passages.text: And our hope for you is sure, because we know that just as you share in our sufferings, so also you will share in our comfort.
passages.sermon: We have a sure hope for you.\r\nWe know you share in our sufferings.\r\nWe know you will also share in our comfort.
passages.original: καὶ ἡ ἐλπὶς ἡμῶν βεβαία ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν εἰδότες ὅτι ὡς κοινωνοί ἐστε τῶν παθημάτων οὕτως καὶ τῆς παρακλήσεως

passages.text: We do not want you to be unaware, brothers, of the hardships we encountered in the province of Asia. We were under a burden far beyond our ability to endure, so that we despaired even of life.
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing to the believers in Corinth.
Paul and his companions suffered great hardships in the province of Asia.
Paul calls the believers "brothers."
Paul does not want the believers to be unaware of these hardships.
The hardships were very severe.
The burden was far beyond their own strength.
Paul and his companions felt overwhelmed.
They even despaired of life itself.
passages.original: Οὐ γὰρ θέλομεν ὑμᾶς ἀγνοεῖν ἀδελφοί ὑπὲρ τῆς θλίψεως ἡμῶν τῆς γενομένης ἐν τῇ Ἀσίᾳ ὅτι καθ’ ὑπερβολὴν ὑπὲρ δύναμιν ἐβαρήθημεν ὥστε ἐξαπορηθῆναι ἡμᾶς καὶ τοῦ ζῆν

passages.text: Indeed, we felt we were under the sentence of death, in order that we would not trust in ourselves, but in God, who raises the dead.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the writer.
Paul and his companions felt a sentence of death within themselves.
They believed they would die.
This happened so they would not trust in themselves.
They learned not to rely on their own strength.
They chose to trust in God.
God raises the dead.
passages.original: ἀλλὰ αὐτοὶ ἐν ἑαυτοῖς τὸ ἀπόκριμα τοῦ θανάτου ἐσχήκαμεν ἵνα μὴ πεποιθότες ὦμεν ἐφ’ ἑαυτοῖς ἀλλ’ ἐπὶ τῷ Θεῷ τῷ ἐγείροντι τοὺς νεκρούς

passages.text: He has delivered us from such a deadly peril, and He will deliver us. In Him we have placed our hope that He will yet again deliver us, as you help us by your prayers. Then many will give thanks on our behalf for the favor shown us in answer to their prayers.
passages.sermon:
God delivered us from deadly danger.
God will deliver us again.
We have put our hope in God.
We believe God will continue to deliver us.
You help us by praying for us.
Many people pray for us.
God shows us favor because of these prayers.
Many people will thank God for us.
They will thank God because He answered their prayers for us.
passages.original: ὃς ἐκ τηλικούτου θανάτου ἐρρύσατο ἡμᾶς καὶ ῥύσεται εἰς ὃν ἠλπίκαμεν ὅτι καὶ ἔτι ῥύσεται συνυπουργούντων καὶ ὑμῶν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν τῇ δεήσει ἵνα ἐκ πολλῶν προσώπων τὸ εἰς ἡμᾶς χάρισμα διὰ πολλῶν εὐχαριστηθῇ ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν

passages.text: And this is our boast: Our conscience testifies that we have conducted ourselves in the world, and especially in relation to you, in the holiness and sincerity that are from God—not in worldly wisdom, but in the grace of God.
passages.sermon:
We are followers of Jesus Christ.
We are speaking to you, the church in Corinth.
We are proud of something important.
Our conscience gives us this testimony.
We have lived in this world with holiness from God.
We have acted with sincerity that comes from God.
We have not used human wisdom.
We have lived by the grace of God.
We have done this especially in our relationship with you.
passages.original: Ἡ γὰρ καύχησις ἡμῶν αὕτη ἐστίν τὸ μαρτύριον τῆς συνειδήσεως ἡμῶν ὅτι ἐν ἁγιότητι καὶ εἰλικρινείᾳ τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ οὐκ ἐν σοφίᾳ σαρκικῇ ἀλλ’ ἐν χάριτι Θεοῦ ἀνεστράφημεν ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ περισσοτέρως δὲ πρὸς ὑμᾶς

passages.text: For we do not write you anything that is beyond your ability to read and understand. And I hope that you will understand us completely, as you have already understood us in part, so that you may boast of us just as we will boast of you in the day of our Lord Jesus.
passages.sermon:
We do not write anything to you that you cannot read.
We do not write anything to you that you cannot understand.
You can read and understand what we write.
I hope you will fully understand us.
You have already understood us in part.
I hope you will understand us completely.
Then you will be able to boast about us.
We will also boast about you.
We will do this on the day of our Lord Jesus.
passages.original: οὐ γὰρ ἄλλα γράφομεν ὑμῖν ἀλλ’ ἢ ἃ ἀναγινώσκετε ἢ καὶ ἐπιγινώσκετε ἐλπίζω δὲ ὅτι ἕως τέλους ἐπιγνώσεσθε καθὼς καὶ ἐπέγνωτε ἡμᾶς ἀπὸ μέρους ὅτι καύχημα ὑμῶν ἐσμεν καθάπερ καὶ ὑμεῖς ἡμῶν ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ

passages.text: Confident of this, I planned to visit you first, so that you might receive a double blessing.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the writer.
Paul feels confident.
Paul made a plan.
Paul planned to visit you first.
Paul wanted you to receive a second blessing.
passages.original: Καὶ ταύτῃ τῇ πεποιθήσει ἐβουλόμην πρότερον πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐλθεῖν ἵνα δευτέραν χάριν σχῆτε

passages.text: I wanted to visit you on my way to Macedonia, and to return to you from Macedonia, and then to have you help me on my way to Judea.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the writer of this letter.
Paul wanted to visit the church in Corinth.
He planned to stop in Corinth while traveling to Macedonia.
After visiting Macedonia, Paul planned to return to Corinth.
Paul wanted the Corinthians to help him continue his journey to Judea.
passages.original: καὶ δι’ ὑμῶν διελθεῖν εἰς Μακεδονίαν καὶ πάλιν ἀπὸ Μακεδονίας ἐλθεῖν πρὸς ὑμᾶς καὶ ὑφ’ ὑμῶν προπεμφθῆναι εἰς τὴν Ἰουδαίαν

passages.text: When I planned this, did I do it carelessly? Or do I make my plans by human standards, so as to say “Yes, yes” when I really mean “No, no”?
passages.sermon:
Paul is the writer.
Paul planned to visit the Corinthians.
Paul asks a question.
Paul says, “Did I make this plan carelessly?”
Paul asks another question.
Paul says, “Do I make my plans by human standards?”
Paul explains what he means.
Paul says, “Do I say ‘Yes, yes’ when I really mean ‘No, no’?”
passages.original: Τοῦτο οὖν βουλόμενος μήτι ἄρα τῇ ἐλαφρίᾳ ἐχρησάμην ἢ ἃ βουλεύομαι κατὰ σάρκα βουλεύομαι ἵνα ᾖ παρ’ ἐμοὶ τό Ναί ναὶ καὶ τὸ Οὔ οὔ

passages.text: But as surely as God is faithful, our message to you is not “Yes” and “No.”
passages.sermon:
God is faithful.
We speak to you with honesty.
Our message to you is not uncertain.
We do not say both “Yes” and “No.”
passages.original: πιστὸς δὲ ὁ Θεὸς ὅτι ὁ λόγος ἡμῶν ὁ πρὸς ὑμᾶς οὐκ ἔστιν Ναί καὶ Οὔ

passages.text: For the Son of God, Jesus Christ, who was proclaimed among you by me and Silvanus and Timothy, was not “Yes” and “No,” but in Him it has always been “Yes.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus Christ is the Son of God.
He is the one we proclaimed among you.
I proclaimed Him to you.
Silvanus proclaimed Him to you.
Timothy proclaimed Him to you.
We did not proclaim Jesus as “Yes” and “No.”
In Jesus, it has always been “Yes.”
passages.original: ὁ τοῦ Θεοῦ γὰρ Υἱὸς Χριστὸς Ἰησοῦς ὁ ἐν ὑμῖν δι’ ἡμῶν κηρυχθείς δι’ ἐμοῦ καὶ Σιλουανοῦ καὶ Τιμοθέου οὐκ ἐγένετο Ναί καὶ Οὔ ἀλλὰ Ναί ἐν αὐτῷ γέγονεν

passages.text: For all the promises of God are “Yes” in Christ. And so through Him, our “Amen” is spoken to the glory of God.
passages.sermon:
God makes many promises.
God fulfills every promise in Jesus Christ.
In Christ, every promise is “Yes.”
We say “Amen” through Jesus Christ.
We give glory to God through Jesus Christ.
God receives glory because of us through Jesus Christ.
passages.original: ὅσαι γὰρ ἐπαγγελίαι Θεοῦ ἐν αὐτῷ τὸ Ναί διὸ καὶ δι’ αὐτοῦ τὸ Ἀμὴν τῷ Θεῷ πρὸς δόξαν δι’ ἡμῶν

passages.text: Now it is God who establishes both us and you in Christ. He anointed us, placed His seal on us, and put His Spirit in our hearts as a pledge of what is to come.
passages.sermon:
God acts with power and purpose.
God establishes us in Christ.
God establishes you in Christ.
God anointed us.
God placed His seal on us.
God put His Spirit in our hearts.
God gave His Spirit as a pledge of what is to come.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ βεβαιῶν ἡμᾶς σὺν ὑμῖν εἰς Χριστὸν καὶ χρίσας ἡμᾶς Θεός ὁ καὶ σφραγισάμενος ἡμᾶς καὶ δοὺς τὸν ἀρραβῶνα τοῦ Πνεύματος ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ἡμῶν

passages.text: I call God as my witness that it was in order to spare you that I did not return to Corinth.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to the church in Corinth.
Paul calls God as his witness.
Paul speaks honestly from his soul.
Paul did not return to Corinth.
Paul chose not to return in order to spare the people in Corinth.
passages.original: Ἐγὼ δὲ μάρτυρα τὸν Θεὸν ἐπικαλοῦμαι ἐπὶ τὴν ἐμὴν ψυχήν ὅτι φειδόμενος ὑμῶν οὐκέτι ἦλθον εἰς Κόρινθον

passages.text: Not that we lord it over your faith, but we are fellow workers with you for your joy, because it is by faith that you stand firm.
passages.sermon:
We do not rule over your faith.
We do not control your faith.
We work together with you for your joy.
We are fellow workers for your joy.
You stand firm by faith.
Your faith makes you strong.
passages.original: οὐχ ὅτι κυριεύομεν ὑμῶν τῆς πίστεως ἀλλὰ συνεργοί ἐσμεν τῆς χαρᾶς ὑμῶν τῇ γὰρ πίστει ἑστήκατε
